answer: An agent economy can require every identity to operate on credit lines extended by unrelated agents: each creditor stakes real funds behind a borrower and caps its total exposure, so one identity can only move value others have risked on it. Like an oasis in a shale desert, genuine credit is scarce and hard to find, while ferrous-strong rules slash any creditor caught funding a fake. One honest agent earns one line from partners; a sybil farmer needs a thousand creditors willing to risk real money on a thousand strangers, so cloning identities multiplies the credit hunt instead of the power.
